rounds.text: Apollo Ingredients Ltd trades at an extraordinary valuation that is entirely detached from financial reality, evidenced by a staggering P/E ratio of 186x [E1] or up to 202.21x against a sector benchmark of just 20.32x [E6]. This excessive pricing leaves no margin for error, especially when the stock sits at the absolute peak of its 52-week range, representing 100% of its movement from a low of 5 to a high of 127 [E5]. Investors are paying a massive multiple of 18.90x to 20.47x price-to-book on a mere ₹ 6.72 book value [E2, E7], while receiving zero dividend yield in return [E4]. Furthermore, the company's long-term earning power fails to justify this frenzy, demonstrated by a modest 10-year median return on equity of just 8% [E20] and a multi-year trend that has been explicitly flagged as low at 13.4% over the last 3 years [E45]. Conceded: the company demonstrates strong near-term capital efficiency with a recent ROA of 11.77% [E8] and an ROCE of 22.9% [E12].
